La respuesta está pasando de las capacidades del modelo en sí a la creación de sistemas inteligentes escalables en torno al modelo; de la mejora de capacidades puntuales a la ingeniería de sistemas y la capacidad de implantación a nivel organizativo.

excerpt_i18n.en: Recently, Shenzhen Chaowei Dongli Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. ("Chaowei Dongli") and Peking University Medical Management Co., Ltd. ("PKU Medical") have reached a deep cooperation. The two parties will jointly innovate around embodied intelligence in medical scenarios, focusing on data collection, world models, and simulation training, and pragmatically build a complete implementation path from "realistic training" to "scene validation" to "hospital application." For embodied intelligence to truly "enter the hospital," it is never as simple as placing a robot directly into a ward. It must first understand the hospital and healthcare workers, then follow the rhythm of "realistic training — validation — application," accumulating capabilities and completing safety verification step by step. This is exactly what Chaowei Dongli and PKU Medical are doing — not rushing for quick results, but first solidifying the foundation and making the path workable. A deep coupling of technology and scenarios: The biggest bottleneck for embodied intelligence in healthcare is "no environment to practice in, no teachers to teach" — lacking both highly realistic medical scenarios and operational data from skilled medical professionals. As a full-stack embodied intelligence large model company, Chaowei Dongli has a complete technology foundation from data collection and world models to highly realistic simulation training. PKU Medical provides the most authentic clinical scenarios and the most professional medical experience. The combination of their strengths makes the pragmatic, verifiable implementation path of "realistic training → scene validation → hospital application" clear and replicable — precisely what scenarios with high safety requirements like healthcare need.

Para que la inteligencia encarnada realmente "entre en el hospital", nunca es tan simple como colocar un robot directamente en una sala de hospital. Primero debe comprender el hospital, comprender al personal médico, y luego avanzar paso a paso siguiendo el ritmo de "simulación - verificación - aplicación".

excerpt_i18n.en:
In Shanghai this July, the buzz around WAIC 2026 might be even louder than the cicadas. Nearly every booth is crowded, with visitors shifting their gaze between the printed boards and exhibitors' faces. Many come here with the same question: where does China’s AI industry truly stand? Leifeng.com has specially planned WAIC 2026 observation reports, speaking with eight decision-makers from participating AI Infra companies to capture what everyone is really focusing on this year from conversations beside the booths, and what new directions and consensus are forming in the industry.  

01 Setting Sail | From Scaling Up to Competing on Efficiency  
This year marks an interesting shift—whether from CEOs or business heads, they all coincidentally mention the same thing: at WAIC 2026, the industry’s focus has changed. In the past, discussions centered on metrics like thousand-card clusters and GPU performance; now, the conversation has turned more toward how to stably and cheaply produce tokens in bulk, and further, how to leverage these stable, low-cost tokens to sustain the stable operation of agents and AI applications.  

Market data clearly validates this transition. In 2025, the total market token call volume surged 300x year-over-year, and growth for leading large-model companies is now entirely driven by API and token calls. Take Zhipu AI as an example: its annualized revenue has jumped from the expected $700 million to $1 billion, with the core of growth coming entirely from inference-side scale.
